name: vllm-startup-warm
description: vLLM 0.33 offline engine, Qwen3.5-9B (8k context, text only), compile caches kept from the warm-up run (a restarted server): process start to first token. Weight load = 19 GB pageable CPU->GPU, one copy per tensor.

name: vllm-startup-cold
description: vLLM 0.33 offline engine, Qwen3.5-9B (8k context, text only), empty compile caches every run (a fresh container: compile and kernel builds included): process start to first token. Weight load = 19 GB pageable CPU->GPU, one copy per tensor.

name: sglang-startup-warm
description: SGLang 0.5.23 offline engine, Qwen3.5-9B (8k context, text only), compile caches kept from the warm-up run (a restarted server): process start to first token. Copies happen in the scheduler child process (not traced).

name: sglang-startup-cold
description: SGLang 0.5.23 offline engine, Qwen3.5-9B (8k context, text only), empty compile caches every run (a fresh container: compile and kernel builds included): process start to first token. Copies happen in the scheduler child process (not traced).

name: sglang-rl-disk-update
description: SGLang 0.5.23 RL weight sync from disk as slime does it (update_weights_from_disk, flush_cache), Qwen3.5-9B (8k context, text only): seconds per full reload of a 19.3 GB checkpoint whose files are in the page cache. Each update copies every loaded tensor pageable (mmap) CPU->GPU: 18.8 GB, counted apart from the file bytes by SGLang's profiler on one extra update, which also splits copy time from SGLang's per-tensor Python. A trainer stand-in writes checkpoints A and B (untimed; the lm_head shard rewritten with two rows swapped, the other shards shared); 5 alternating updates per run, each verified by greedy generation. Copies happen in the scheduler child process (not traced).

name: vllm-sleep-l1
description: vLLM sleep level 1 x3 cycles (RL rollout pattern), Qwen3.5-9B. Weights backed up to pinned CPU memory: all weights GPU->CPU and back per cycle; the first sleep pins ~1.3x the weight bytes.

name: vllm-sleep-l1-pageable
description: The same sleep level 1 x3 cycles with the weight backup in pageable memory, vLLM's default under WSL2 (pin_memory off unless VLLM_WSL2_ENABLE_PIN_MEMORY=1): each sleep copies the weights GPU->CPU into fresh pageable memory and each wake copies them back.

name: vllm-sleep-l2
description: vLLM sleep level 2 + reload_weights x3 cycles, Qwen3.5-9B. Each reload copies the 19 GB of safetensors pageable CPU->GPU.

name: hf-load
description: Transformers from_pretrained(device_map='cuda'), Qwen3-8B bf16: 16.4 GB pageable (mmap) CPU->GPU, one copy per tensor.

name: hf-offload
description: Transformers big-model inference (device_map='auto', 3 GiB GPU budget), Qwen3-8B: every token streams the CPU-resident layers as pageable CPU->GPU copies.

name: checkpoint-save-torch251
description: torch.save of a GPT-2-large training state (fp32 + AdamW, 9.3 GB), Torch 2.5.1: pageable GPU->CPU copy per tensor, up to 257 MB. In-memory file, so the disk is not measured. Torch 2.5.1 has no Blackwell (sm_120) code: the torch251 entries stop with that reason there.

name: checkpoint-load-torch251
description: torch.load(map_location='cuda') + load_state_dict of the same 9.3 GB state (nanoGPT resume), Torch 2.5.1: pageable CPU->GPU copy per tensor.

name: checkpoint-async-torch251
description: torch.distributed.checkpoint.async_save (default writer) of the 9.3 GB state, Torch 2.5.1: blocking time to stage to CPU with pageable .to('cpu') copies.

name: checkpoint-async-torch
description: The same async_save with Torch 2.14.1 (cu130), whose staging may differ from 2.5.1. Runs on Blackwell, unlike the torch251 entries.

name: dataloader-imagenette
description: ResNet-50 training on Imagenette JPEGs, DataLoader default pin_memory=False: one 154 MB pageable CPU->GPU batch per step.

name: dataloader-imagenette-pinned
description: Reference for dataloader-imagenette: pin_memory=True (torchvision reference recipe). Batches are pinned, so the hook should change nothing.

name: activation-offload
description: ResNet-152 training, batch 128, with torch.autograd.graph.save_on_cpu() (default pin_memory=False): every saved activation goes GPU->CPU and back, pageable.

name: tensors-torch
description: PyTorch x.to('cuda') and y.cpu() of pageable tensors, 16 MB / 256 MB / 1 GB, 5 each per direction.

name: tensors-jax
description: JAX jax.device_put(numpy) and np.asarray(jax.Array), 16 MB / 256 MB / 1 GB, 5 each per direction.

name: cudf-polars-pdsh
description: cudf-polars PDS-H SF10 queries 1,3,9,13,18,21, streaming engine with a 2 GiB device budget (spills to its default pinned host pool); parquet input and spill copies both ways.
